result:
The fix has landed on PR #78's branch.

## Summary

Root cause: `audit_and_correct_plan_file()`'s while-loop reverted violations one at a time, re-reading the mutated on-disk file each iteration but blaming line numbers against `git blame HEAD` — where HEAD still pointed at the pre-revert commit since the revert hadn't been committed yet. A revert that deletes lines (when the parent lacks `completed_by_task`/`evidence`) desyncs subsequent line numbers, causing `git blame` to attribute the wrong commit to the next violation — in the reviewer's reproduction, landing on the repo's root commit and getting back a corrupted `^`-prefixed hash.

Fix: replaced the one-at-a-time loop with `find_all_unverified_done_blocks()` (finds every violation in a single pass) plus resolving all blame/parent lookups against one unmutated `lines` snapshot before any revert, then applying all reverts bottom-to-top in one pass. Also fixed the secondary gap: `commit_and_push_audit()` now persists (via `--allow-empty` when nothing was reverted) whenever any incident is found, so found-but-uncorrected violations no longer vanish silently.

Added `scenario_audit_reverts_two_violations_in_one_file`, verified it fails against the pre-fix code (reproducing the exact corrupted-hash failure) and passes against the fix. Full suite: 11/11 passing. Pushed directly to PR #78's branch as instructed — not merged, awaiting fresh audit.
